correctness.rationale: Bernshteyn's Theorem 1.1 gives chi_B^*=1/alpha_beta and Lemma 2.2 gives arbitrarily close clopen independent sets. Clopen cylinders have finite support; lifting cylinders along an increasing exhaustion preserves measure and independence, so the finite optima increase to alpha_beta. Decidable group equality makes every finite cylinder-intersection test decidable, and the finite-degree Borel coloring bound supplies a total initial rational upper bound.

value.rationale: The result converts an infinite Borel invariant into a canonical monotone sequence of finite rational optimization problems for every effectively presented countably infinite group with decidable equality. It yields a genuine computability classification (right-c.e.) and identifies a sharp algorithmic boundary without claiming an efficient algorithm or full computability.
